candidates.name: Storm in Gironde Coast, France
candidates.reason:

Copernicus EMS On-Demand Rapid Mapping was requested to provide Delineation extent  and damage assessment emergency mapping

The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported at least 60 people have been killed following the flash flooding that affected 20 villages and damaged a further 50 after the dam's collapse. It is estimated 50,000 people had been severely affected by the disaster. Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping is requested to provide flood extent and damage assessment emergency mapping.

candidates.name: Flood in Norway
candidates.reason: On the 22 May 2023, there is an ongoing spring flood in several parts of Norway due to snow melt from winter with an high amount of snowfall. Some rivers in southeast of Norway and some places in northern Norway (Finnmark) have high discharge and rain is forecasted in in some places. Some rivers will probably peak very soon, today or tomorrow, while other rivers probably will peak in 2 to 3 days, depending on temperature and rainfall.

candidates.name: Flood in Bosnia and Herzegovina
candidates.reason: Heavy rain affecting Bosnia and Herzegovina caused flooding in the northern part of the country. A state of emergency has been declared in several cities and municipalities. In several communities around Sana and Una rivers, buildings and houses have been flooded. Landslides have been triggered by the floods. Due to water overflows, the traffic on several roads has been interrupted. Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping is requested to provide flood extent and damage assessment emergency mapping.

candidates.name: Flood in Italy
candidates.reason: A new wave of severe weather has again hit south-eastern areas of the Emilia-Romagna region, Italy. The same area was faced with floods already on 2 May 2023, which resulted in three deaths. The accompanying rains also caused landslides in the middle Apennines area of this region, which left hundreds of people displaced. On 16 May 2023, a new perturbation has raised river levels. The hydrometric threshold was reached in the basins of the Idice, Samoggia, Savio, Marzeno, Voltre, Marecchia, Pisciatello, Ausa, and Montone rivers. New floods are expected in the areas as well as possible evacuation

candidates.name: Flood in Mozambique
candidates.reason: Following Cyclone Freddy several communities in central and northern provinces of Mozambique have been totally isolated. In the framework of the emergency response, WFP is planning to provide food assistance to a community particularly impacted by floods located in an area that is being reported as being accessible only via motorbike. An informal refugee camp has been established in the area and WFP needs to access the status of the roads in the proximity of the camp and identify potential access routes for trucks.

candidates.name: Flood in Uganda
candidates.reason: River Katonga in Western Uganda flooded on the morning of Thursday 11th May 2023 after heavy rain and submerged the major trans-national road connecting the central and northern part of the country to the western and south-western parts of the country as well as to Rwanda, Burundi and DR Congo. By close of the day, the bridge had been washed away.  Local media reports said the Katonga Bridge over the River Katonga on the Kampala-Masaka highway in Mpigi District was destroyed and motorists were forced to take a detour of 50 km or more.

candidates.name: Flood in Daugava River valley, Latvia
candidates.reason:
As of 30 March 2023 a flood due to melted snow and ice, as well as precipitation has been observed in the Daugava river valley, Latvia.
It is forecasted that in the upcoming days due to the precipitation water level in the Daugava river and its tributaries will keep rising flooding larger areas. The evacuation of the area in proximity to the to the river is foreseen.
Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping is requested to provide the flood extent with daily update until the end of the event and a final damage assessment.
